```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>",
  eval = FALSE

```

orcidtr reads public data from ORCID records and returns each section as a data.table. The code in this vignette is not run when the vignette is built, because it needs the ORCID API; run it yourself to see the output.

The examples use three records: Josiah Carberry (`0000-0002-1825-0097`), a fictitious researcher whose record ORCID keeps for demonstrations; Hadley Wickham (`0000-0003-4757-117X`); and Martin Fenner (`0000-0003-1419-2405`).

```{r setup}
library(orcidtr)
library(data.table)
```

## One section of one record

Each section of a record has its own function. It takes an ORCID iD, with or without dashes or an `https://orcid.org/` prefix, and returns one row per item. A section the researcher has left empty gives a zero-row table with the same columns, so filtering and binding code does not need a special case for it.

```{r sections}
person <- orcid_person("0000-0003-4757-117X")
person[, .(given_names, family_name, country)]

employments <- orcid_employments("0000-0003-4757-117X")
employments[, .(organization, role, start_date, end_date)]

orcid_educations("0000-0003-4757-117X")
orcid_keywords("0000-0003-4757-117X")
```

Works carry their type, publication date, journal and DOI. Dates are strings in ISO order (`"2014"`, `"2014-08"` or `"2014-08-29"`) because ORCID often records only the year or the month, so they sort correctly as text:

```{r works}
works <- orcid_works("0000-0003-4757-117X")
works[, .N, by = type][order(-N)]

recent <- works[order(publication_date, decreasing = TRUE)]
head(recent[, .(title, type, publication_date, doi)], 5)

works[, year := as.integer(substr(publication_date, 1, 4))]
works[!is.na(year), .N, by = year][order(year)]
```

Funding, peer reviews and the remaining affiliation types follow the same pattern:

```{r activities}
orcid_funding("0000-0003-1419-2405")
orcid_peer_reviews("0000-0002-1825-0097")
orcid_distinctions("0000-0003-1419-2405")
orcid_memberships("0000-0003-1419-2405")
```

## Several sections or several records

`orcid_fetch_record()` sends one request per section and returns a named list. The default sections are employments, educations, works, funding and peer reviews; `sections` selects others. A section whose request fails becomes an empty table and a warning, so one failure does not lose the rest.

```{r fetch-record}
record <- orcid_fetch_record(
  "0000-0003-4757-117X",
  sections = c("works", "employments", "person")
)
names(record)
record$person
```

`orcid_activities()` gets the summaries of every activity section in a single request. It is the cheaper choice when you need several sections of one record:

```{r activities-summary}
activities <- orcid_activities("0000-0003-4757-117X")
vapply(activities, nrow, integer(1))
```

`orcid_fetch_many()` fetches one section for many records and binds the rows, with the `orcid` column saying which record each row came from. Invalid iDs and failed requests produce warnings and are skipped unless `stop_on_error = TRUE`:

```{r fetch-many}
orcids <- c(
  "0000-0003-4757-117X",
  "0000-0002-1825-0097",
  "0000-0003-1419-2405"
)
all_works <- orcid_fetch_many(orcids, section = "works")
all_works[, .N, by = orcid]
all_works[publication_date >= "2020", .N, by = orcid]
```

## Searching the registry

`orcid_search()` builds a query from named fields and combines them with `AND`. Values with spaces are quoted for you, so `affiliation_org = "Stanford University"` matches that phrase. Several keywords match any of them.

```{r search}
orcid_search(family_name = "Wickham", given_name = "Hadley")
orcid_search(affiliation_org = "Stanford University", rows = 20)
orcid_search(keywords = c("psychoceramics", "ionian philology"))
```

`orcid()` sends a raw [Solr query](https://info.orcid.org/documentation/api-tutorials/api-tutorial-searching-the-orcid-registry/). Here you quote multi-word values yourself: unquoted, `affiliation-org-name:Stanford University` also matches every record that mentions "University" anywhere. The `found` attribute gives the total number of matches, and `start` pages through them.

```{r solr}
results <- orcid(
  'keyword:"machine learning" AND affiliation-org-name:"Harvard University"',
  rows = 50
)
attr(results, "found")

page2 <- orcid('keyword:"machine learning"', rows = 50, start = 50)
```

`orcid_doi()` finds the records that list a DOI among their works. With several DOIs it returns a list named by DOI, and `fuzzy = TRUE` treats each DOI as a prefix:

```{r doi}
orcid_doi("10.1371/journal.pone.0025995")
orcid_doi(c("10.1038/nature12373", "10.1126/science.1260419"))
orcid_doi("10.1371/journal.pone", fuzzy = TRUE, rows = 20)
```

## Limits and tokens

ORCID limits anonymous use of the public API to 12 requests a second, with up to 40 queued, and to 25,000 reads a day from each IP address. Registering a public API client and using its `/read-public` token raises the daily quota to 100,000 reads per client; the per-second rate stays the same. These are the figures on [ORCID's API limits page](https://info.orcid.org/ufaqs/what-are-the-api-limits/) as of November 2026.

orcidtr sends requests one after another and tries a request up to three times when ORCID answers 429 or 503, which it does when the queue is full. A batch of a few hundred records needs no extra care. For a batch that approaches the daily quota, get a token: register a public API client in your ORCID account's developer tools, then exchange its client ID and secret for a token.

```{r token}
library(httr2)

token <- request("https://orcid.org/oauth/token") |>
  req_headers(Accept = "application/json") |>
  req_body_form(
    client_id = "YOUR-CLIENT-ID",
    client_secret = "YOUR-CLIENT-SECRET",
    grant_type = "client_credentials",
    scope = "/read-public"
  ) |>
  req_perform() |>
  resp_body_json()

works <- orcid_works("0000-0003-4757-117X", token = token$access_token)
```

The token lasts about twenty years. No function reads it from the environment, because the public API rejects an invalid token even though it needs none, so a stale token left in `.Renviron` would break every call. If you keep one there, pass it explicitly with `token = Sys.getenv("ORCID_TOKEN")`.

A token does not reveal more of a record. The public API returns only what the researcher has made public; data with limited visibility needs the researcher's permission through the Member API, which this package does not use. For this reason `orcid_email()` usually returns an empty table.

## Errors

A malformed iD fails before any request is sent. A record that does not exist, a rejected token and an exhausted quota each stop with a message naming the cause. `orcid_ping()` tells you whether the API itself is up:

```{r errors}
orcid_ping()

result <- tryCatch(
  orcid_works("0000-0000-0000-0000"),
  error = function(e) {
    message(conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  }
)
```
